environmentalPersistence: Moderate — half-life ~47 days in soil; binds tightly to soil particles; metabolized to AMPA

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Very strong — EPSPS inhibition blocks aromatic amino acid synthesis; growth ceases completely at effective doses
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Moderate — distorted new growth is most visible symptom
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Strong — tissue death from amino acid starvation
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strong — chloroplast development blocked without Phe/Tyr/Trp supply
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Strong — complete tissue death at effective doses; characteristic browning from meristematic tissue outward
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Mild — insufficient biochemical capacity for anthocyanin without aromatic amino acids
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Severely inhibited — systemic herbicide reaches roots
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: New growth most affected (requires active amino acid synthesis); old leaves yellowing follows

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Strong — EPSPS inhibition secondary effects include ROS accumulation
molecularEffects.anthocyaninInduction: Minimal — aromatic amino acid pathway (shikimate) is the exact target; anthocyanin synthesis requires this pathway
defenseProteins: minimal — aromatic AA pathway for PR proteins is blocked

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Strong — glyphosate has significant broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties
microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Strongly suppressed — PGPR containing EPSPS are sensitive; only glyphosate-resistant strains survive
microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Disrupted — beneficial fungi suppressed; Fusarium (pathogen) reportedly increases

firstSymptoms: yellowing and distortion of newest leaves
temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: None at effective herbicide doses — designed for complete plant kill

visualSimulation.colorChanges: New growth yellows first → pale white/yellow → brown necrosis spreading from apex downward
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Apical meristem and newest leaves — most metabolically active tissue
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Apex downward — opposite of senescence (which goes old-to-young)
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Apex-to-base progression is diagnostic for glyphosate vs other herbicides
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Strong amber — shikimate accumulation and AMPA metabolite are diagnostic; shikimate peak is pathognomonic for EPSPS inhibition
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Strongly reduced; high pathogen fraction; resistome elevated

synergies.synergyNote: Glyphosate + atrazine combination herbicide use is common and produces complete multi-mechanism knockdown — EPSPS inhibition + photosystem II inhibition together are more effective than either alone

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Roundup (Monsanto/Bayer) and hundreds of generic formulations — most widely used herbicide globally; ~800,000 tonnes applied per year
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: GMO Roundup-Ready crop systems; weed control in no-till agriculture; pre-harvest desiccation of wheat and oats
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Highly contested — IARC classified as Group 2A (probable carcinogen) 2015; EPA maintains it is not carcinogenic. Major ongoing legal and scientific controversy.
educationalContext.climateLink: No-till agriculture using glyphosate stores more carbon in soil — complex tradeoff between herbicide use and carbon sequestration
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Outdoor — residential lawns, roadsides, agriculture; residues in food
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: The most controversial pesticide in the world — GMO crops, cancer lawsuits ($10B+ in settlements), weed resistance, food safety debates. One of the most fertile topics for scientific evidence evaluation.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: GMO agriculture, weed resistance crisis, cancer controversy, food residue safety
